comments.author: @KayG-x3q
comments.text:
Whilst day trading involves an element of risk, it amounts to  lazy thinking to cast it in the same mould as gambling, which relies purely on luck. Trading requires an in-depth understanding of economics and politics as well sharp analytical skills. Of course, being proficient in these skills will not immunize you from loss but will definitely tip the balance in your favor in the long-term, much as having done a thorough analysis of the market you're entering in business, ie: demand vs supply, competition etc.. will not guarantee that your business succeeds. It just gives you an edge.

That said, I've come to realize that most day traders don't do the heavy background work. They think a chart alone will determine direction. Without contradicting myself, while trading is far from it being gambling, the majority of traders go into it with a gambling mentality: No fundamental analysis, take-all- or-nothing, which then explains the 98% failure rate. Risk management comes first. Thinking in terms of probabilities rather than certainly. Small consistent profits are more feasible than quick large profits that will be reversed the very next trading session.
